title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey Sign a New Defense Pact
gist: A Warcast episode note flags that on Aug. 7, 2026 the leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, previewing a discussion with Michael Kugelman on what each country brings to the pact, their shared interests, and how they are balancing it against relations with Washington.

insights.claim: On Aug. 7, 2026, the leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, a new trilateral defense pact.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: A new, named trilateral security pact (Mecca Joint Defense Agreement) among three significant regional military powers is a structural realignment worth tracking for its implications on Gulf security architecture, arms flows, and each country's bilateral ties with the U.S.

insights.claim: The episode examines what each of the three countries (Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan) brings to the agreement and their shared interests, indicating the pact rests on complementary rather than symmetric capabilities among the signatories.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Suggests the pact should be read as a capability-pooling arrangement (e.g., Pakistan's nuclear/military manpower, Turkey's defense-industrial base, Saudi financing) rather than a simple alliance of equals.

insights.claim: The three signatory countries are described as working to maintain relations with Washington while simultaneously looking toward regional security arrangements outside the traditional U.S.-centered framework.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Signals a broader trend of key U.S. partners hedging toward regional/multilateral security arrangements alongside (not instead of) the U.S. relationship — relevant to assessing the durability of traditional U.S. Gulf and South Asia alliance structures.
